audit.why: Emerald+ win rate 47.17% over 884 games (MC_REAL_GAMES.trundle.sett). The audit packet reports games:null for this matchup only — 70 of 71 entries have games — so the packet field is stale, not the data.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Trundle 3 stages and Sett 0 while the lane is a 47.17% loss for Trundle. The content win[] and the full phases[].side agreed with each other but both contradicted the win rate; the packet flagged it as a defect.
audit.why: Sett owns levels 1-3: Knuckle Down deals damage based on the target's max health and is untouched by Chomp's AD steal, Haymaker lands at 2 with a shield plus a true-damage centre, and his level-3 Facebreaker into Knuckle Down into Haymaker sequence beats anything Trundle has before Subjugate. Trundle's edge is ultimate and item scaling, not the laning phase.
audit.corrected: Sett / Sett / Sett / Skill / Skill / Trundle / Trundle, ratings 4,3,3,5,5,7,7. Proposed as one atomic group across both layers.
sources: packet defect: level chart contradicts data

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text put the swing at 'Lvl 1-2' on a nonexistent attack-speed steal and framed level 6 as Sett's window alone.
audit.why: The real spikes are Sett's Haymaker at 2 (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s) and his level-3 combo, then Trundle's Subjugate at 6 and Iceborn Gauntlet. Both ultimates are 120/100/80; Subjugate's 650 range beats The Show Stopper's 400, which is what makes level 6 a coin-flip rather than a loss.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[0] and spikes[2] with real cooldowns and ranges; whys[4] and phases[4].why now key level 6 to the range gap and to opening fights with R because the steal doubles over 4 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four factual errors in the ability interactions. (a) Chomp was repeatedly described as stealing ATTACK SPEED and slowing Pit Grit's punch cadence — Riot's text says it saps Attack Damage. (b) Haymaker was described as a cast Sett must 'stand still and channel', interruptible by Pillar of Ice — nothing in the kit supports a channel, and Pillar creates terrain, it does not interrupt. (c) Facebreaker was described flatly as a stun — Riot's text stuns only enemies caught on opposite sides of Sett; a lone target is slowed. (d) Subjugate's stolen Armor and MR were said to absorb Haymaker's true-damage panel — true damage ignores resistances by definition.
audit.why: Each changes what the player does. (a) decides whether the AD steal blunts Knuckle Down — it does not, that is max-health damage. (b) removes a counterplay that does not exist and replaces it with the real one, baiting an 18s cooldown. (c) is the highest-value fact in the matchup: solo, Facebreaker is a slow, and it is Trundle's own wave that supplies the far-side body converting it into a stun. (d) stops the player expecting the R steal to cover the punch centre.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0..6], early, mid, late, spikes[0], spikes[2], wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], phases[0..4].why and dontsFull[1].d to state the AD (not AS) steal, the both-sides Facebreaker condition, Haymaker's Grit-from-damage-taken loop and 18s cooldown, and the true-damage limit on the Subjugate steal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Riot descriptions for Pit Grit, Knuckle Down, Haymaker, Facebreaker, The Show Stopper)
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (Chomp, Frozen Domain, Pillar of Ice, Subjugate)

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice told the player to force extended fights inside Frozen Domain against Sett.
audit.why: Haymaker stores Grit from damage Sett takes, so the longer the trade the bigger his shield and true-damage punch. The correct pattern is short trades that bait Haymaker, then commit in its 18s window.
audit.corrected: early, whys[1] and phases[1].why now say the poke charges Haymaker and to trade short until it is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers marked the punishable windows.
audit.why: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10 are the two windows that decide the lane, and Chomp's 3.5s cooldown is why the AD steal can be kept up.
audit.corrected: All three cooldowns now appear in the rewritten spikes, whys, early and phases text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful hidden mechanic — that Facebreaker's stun needs bodies on both sides, and that Trundle's own minion wave is what supplies one — appeared nowhere.
audit.why: It is the difference between a 16-second stun and a slow, and it is entirely under the player's control through positioning.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[3], mid, phases[3].why, wants.foe[1] and dontsFull[1].d.

edits.before: Chomp's attack-speed steal hits Sett on the opening trade — his passive double-punch loses half its tempo the moment his AS drops.
edits.after: Chomp saps Attack Damage, not attack speed — a 3.5s cooldown lets you re-apply it every trade, so each Pit Grit punch comes back weaker.

edits.before: Sett's Showstopper is his equaliser — if he gets the suppress off into a wall or your wave, he converts it directly into a full Haymaker. Respect this window and keep the Pillar ready to cut his approach.
edits.after: Both ultimates are 120/100/80, but Subjugate reaches 650 and The Show Stopper only 400 — so R him from outside his grab range the moment he steps up, and keep Pillar of Ice on the ground he has to walk over to reach you.

edits.before: Stack Chomp's AD steal early so his Haymaker true-damage panel is drawing from a diminished AD pool
edits.after: Bait Haymaker before you commit — it is 18s at rank 1 and his shield and true-damage punch die with it

edits.before: Land Facebreaker to stun you mid-Frozen Domain so your W healing window is wasted
edits.after: Angle Facebreaker so your minion is on his far side — that upgrades the slow to a stun

edits.before: Chomp's attack-speed steal lands on the very first trade — Sett's passive double-punch loses pace immediately and your King's Tribute heal from minion deaths offsets his auto damage before either of you has abilities.
edits.after: Chomp saps Attack Damage, not attack speed — Pit Grit punches hit softer but keep their cadence, and Knuckle Down's max-health damage is untouched by the steal, so his level-1 exchange still out-damages your King's Tribute chip healing.

edits.before: Frozen Domain at level 2 makes you the aggressor: you move faster and heal faster inside it than he can trade back, and he has no early escape from a placed W zone.
edits.after: Haymaker lands at 2 and your Frozen Domain poke is what charges it — every Chomp and auto you land banks Grit into his shield and true-damage centre. Trade short here, not long.

edits.before: With Q, W, and E online you can Chomp his AD down, sustain through his grit-banked trades, and Pillar the exit so he eats the full Domain fight — this is your clearest winning window.
edits.after: Sett's level-3 sequence is the lane's peak: Facebreaker into Knuckle Down into a Grit-fed Haymaker. Facebreaker is 16s at rank 1 and that gap, not your Domain, is the window you trade in.

edits.before: Sett looks for short burst sequences at levels 4-5 to avoid the prolonged heal war; respect the Facebreaker grab angle and commit only when his E is on cooldown.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns if it catches enemies on both sides of him — solo, you are only slowed. Stand on the side away from your own wave and his 16s stun is just a slow.

edits.before: Showstopper comes online and flips the threat level — one suppress into a wall converts to a full Haymaker true-damage burst; keep Pillar ready to interrupt his approach.
edits.after: The Show Stopper carries you off your own ice, which is the one thing that beats Frozen Domain — hold Pillar of Ice for the walk-up, since at 400 range he has to close the gap on foot.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet Spellblade slow stacks on top of Frozen Domain speed, making him permanently stuck inside your zone — sustained Chomp trades drain his AD while you heal through his burst.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's chill stacks with Chomp's slow and Frozen Domain's speed, so Sett cannot walk out of your zone — and he has no dash to leave it, only a 400-range Show Stopper.

edits.before: Neither kit decisively outscales the other, but Subjugate on an armor-stacking Sett tips team fights cleanly in your favour; respect a full-build Showstopper opener in side-lane 1v1s.
edits.after: Subjugate steals a percent of Health, Armor and MR and doubles it over 4 seconds, so an HP-and-resist Sett is your best target on the map — open fights with it rather than saving it.

edits.before: At level 1, open with Q Chomp on the first auto trade — the attack-speed steal immediately cuts into Sett's passive double-punch cadence, and any nearby minion death primes your King's Tribute heal to offset his return damage. Take W at level 2 and place Frozen Domain directly in the middle of the minion wave before walking into him: inside that zone you move faster, heal faster, and attack faster than he does, and Chomp's recurring AD steal means each double-punch he throws back is slightly weaker than the last. He will try to bank grit off your poke to charge Haymaker — that is fine, because a full Haymaker requires him to stand still and channel the cast, and E Pillar of Ice goes down to interrupt his step-in. By level 3 with Q, W, and E all online you own this interaction decisively: commit only inside the Domain, drop Pillar behind him so he cannot simply walk away, and let the sustained healing from passive and W do the rest.
edits.after: At level 1, open Chomp on the first auto exchange — it saps his Attack Damage, not his attack speed, so Pit Grit keeps its cadence but every punch lands lighter, and a nearby minion death primes King's Tribute to offset his return damage. Do not read this as a level-1 win: Knuckle Down deals damage off your max health and ignores the AD steal entirely, so his opener still beats yours. Take W at level 2 and place Frozen Domain under your feet for the move speed, attack speed and increased healing — but understand what your poke is buying him. Haymaker banks Grit from the damage Sett takes, so every Chomp and auto you land is charging his shield and the true-damage centre of his punch. Poke him and leave; do not stand in a heal war feeding that bar. Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 seconds and it is not a channel you can interrupt — the counterplay is baiting it out and fighting in the gap after. By level 3 both kits are complete and his is the stronger all-in, so commit only when Facebreaker and Haymaker are both down.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 Sett starts respecting the sustain and may try shorter burst trades — auto, Q, auto, Facebreaker grab — to stun you before your Frozen Domain ticks become overwhelming. Keep the Domain placement honest and dodge the Facebreaker angle by sidestepping his walk-up; once his E is on cooldown you have a clean window to commit. At level 6 the dynamic shifts slightly: Sett's Showstopper suppresses you and can dump you into your own wave or a wall before releasing the Haymaker follow-up. Respect the R window — save Pillar of Ice to place it between you and his approach path so he cannot close the gap cleanly. If Subjugate comes up first, use it immediately on a moderate-trade opening rather than saving it for a perfect all-in; the armor steal alone tips every subsequent Frozen Domain trade in your favour and his Haymaker true damage starts pulling from a defense pool he no longer fully owns.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 hinge on one rule most players get wrong: Facebreaker pulls in enemies on opposite sides of Sett and only stuns if it catches them on both sides. Alone against him it is a slow, not a stun — so the danger is your own wave. Fight from the side he has nothing behind him on, and a 16-second stun becomes an inconvenience. Once his E is spent you have a clean window to plant Frozen Domain and commit. At level 6 The Show Stopper carries you off your ice and slams you somewhere of his choosing, which is the one thing that genuinely beats your W zone. Subjugate answers it at 650 range against his 400, and both ultimates run 120/100/80 — so cast yours as he walks in, not after he lands. Open with it rather than saving it: the Health, Armor and MR steal doubles over 4 seconds, so it is worth roughly twice as much at the start of a fight as at the end. Note the limit — stolen resists do nothing against Haymaker's true-damage centre.

edits.before: In the late game both kits reach their ceiling at a similar pace — your Iceborn Gauntlet Spellblade slow and his Titan's Resolve or Heartsteel stacking mean neither of you is a clean 1v1 favourite anymore. Your Subjugate remains the decisive team-fight lever: casting it on a bruiser-Sett who has built armor and HP strips those stats onto you and turns a tank-adjacent fight into one you dominate. In side-lane 1v1 duels at 2-plus items, respect a Showstopper that opens with a wall slam into immediate Haymaker — that sequence can kill you through your own healing if he is full-build. The play is to force the fight on your terms: Frozen Domain down, Pillar blocking his exit, Subjugate before the Haymaker lands so your resistance pool absorbs the true-damage panel from a higher base.
edits.after: Late, Titan's Resolve or Heartsteel push Sett past you in a straight brawl, but that same build makes him the best Subjugate target on the map — the steal is a percent of his Health, Armor and MR, so the fatter he gets the more you take. Know what it does not cover: Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the resists you drain off him only blunt the physical damage on the sides of the punch. Sidestep the middle. In side-lane duels at two-plus items, respect an opener of The Show Stopper into an immediate Haymaker — that sequence kills you through your healing. Force the fight on your terms instead: Frozen Domain down, Pillar of Ice between you so he walks the long way, and Subjugate cast at 650 range before he reaches grab distance.

edits.before: Chomp start — bite Sett on every last-hit attempt. The flat damage plus AD steal wins almost every level-1 exchange.
edits.after: Chomp start, bite every last-hit — but it saps AD, not attack speed, and Knuckle Down's max-health damage ignores it.

edits.before: W down at your feet turns short trades your way: move speed, attack speed, and healing on your own terrain. Trade only inside the zone.
edits.after: Haymaker online, and your poke charges it: Grit banks from damage Sett takes, so a long trade hands him the shield and true-damage punch.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Sett to deny disengage, or between you and Haymaker to break his pattern.
edits.after: Both kits complete and his all-in is stronger: Facebreaker into Knuckle Down into Haymaker. Trade in the 16s E gap.

edits.before: Q ranks raise the bite damage and the AD steal. Keep trading in W; if Sett stands in your domain trading evenly, he is losing.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides of him; solo you are slowed. Fight away from your wave and Pillar his angle.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Sett commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Subjugate reaches 650 against The Show Stopper's 400, both 120/100/80 — R him on the walk-up. Open with it: the Health, Armor and MR steal doubles over 4s.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Solo it is only a slow — it stuns when your own wave sits on his far side.

notes: PACKET DEFECT: tools/audit-run/packets/trundle.json has games:null for sett only (the other 70 of 71 entries are populated) while champ-data/content/trundle.js MC_REAL_GAMES.trundle.sett = 884. In MC_REAL_GAMES the sett key is appended last in the object, which is likely why the packet builder missed it. This matchup was therefore NOT deferred. — The packet's levelChart for sett (Trundle,Trundle,Trundle,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill) matches neither shipped chart (both were Skill,Skill,Skill,Trundle,Skill,Trundle,Trundle), so the packet chart looks stale and the fix was made against the shipped charts, which did agree with each other. — The three suspectNames were all false positives: 'Frozen Domain', 'Pillar of Ice' and 'Subjugate' are the real Riot names; the near-miss was caused by adjacent words being caught in the snippet. — Left diff/diffRating/carryRating unchanged: 'HARD' paired with 4/10 reads oddly, but the identical pairing appears on aatrox, malphite, nasus, darius, sejuani and tryndamere, so it is a champion-wide convention rather than a sett-specific error. — tldr repeats 'bite his AD and out-duel him in your W' twice in consecutive sentences; not false, so not edited, but it reads badly. — No mirror existed: audits/top/sett__trundle.json is absent, so nothing was reused and nothing should conflict.
